families.axis: unchanging as a bare fact → steadiness that never tires

members.gloss: steadfast in purpose or devotion or affection
members.tone: Straightforward praise for not wavering, and it covers purpose, devotion and affection alike rather than loyalty alone.

members.gloss: firm and dependable especially in loyalty
members.tone: Weightier than *constant* because it adds dependability, making the firmness something others can lean on.

members.gloss: constant and unchanging
members.tone: Absolute and cool: it reports that a thing does not change rather than crediting it with holding fast, so no praise attaches the way it does to *steadfast*.

members.gloss: tireless
members.tone: Approving of what never runs out, measuring steadiness by supply rather than by the refusal to vary that *constant* asks for.

members.gloss: tireless
members.tone: The same tirelessness as *unfailing*, but figured as a pace that never slackens rather than a store that never empties.

families.axis: a passing piece of bad luck → an event of ruinous loss

members.gloss: an unfortunate development
members.tone: The lightest way here to mark a thing having gone wrong — regret at the turn events took, with no weight of loss behind it.

members.gloss: an unfortunate development
members.tone: Meets the same unfortunate turn as *pity* with a sharper note of protest, as though the outcome were one that need not have happened.

members.gloss: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
members.tone: Lifts the scale abruptly out of bad luck into great loss, and does it more bluntly than *catastrophe*.

members.gloss: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
members.tone: The same great loss as *disaster*, pitched as total and past reversing, with nothing left to salvage.

members.gloss: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
members.tone: Loads the great loss with grief and waste, asking that it be mourned rather than merely counted up.

members.gloss: an instance of misfortune
members.tone: Shrinks misfortune to one small instance, a thing to be shrugged off rather than suffered.

members.gloss: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
members.tone: Ruin on the scale of *disaster* but declared in a grander, more sonorous register.

members.gloss: something that causes or entails suffering
members.tone: Covers both what inflicts the suffering and the suffering entailed, a weight borne over time where *mishap* is over in a moment.

members.gloss: a bad experience
members.tone: Blunt and physical, casting a bad experience as a single blow taken and absorbed.

members.gloss: an instance of misfortune
members.tone: The more formal twin of *mishap*, putting the weight on the luck of the thing rather than the damage done.

families.axis: sexual morality named as conduct → sexual morality named as a woman's standing

members.gloss: morality with respect to sexual relations
members.tone: Approving but plain, naming sexual conduct as a moral good in itself without *honour*'s sense of a reputation that can be taken away.

members.gloss: a woman's virtue or chastity
members.tone: Raises a woman's chastity to a matter of standing — something she is credited with and can be stripped of — where *virtue* only calls it moral; British spelling of *honor*.

members.gloss: a woman's virtue or chastity
members.tone: The same weighted word as *honour* in its American spelling: a woman's chastity treated as her good name rather than as conduct.

members.gloss: accept as true
members.tone: Blunt and informal where *believe* is plain, it treats accepting a claim as taking something on offer, so the acceptance sounds weighed rather than simply held.

members.gloss: accept as true; take to be true
members.tone: The unmarked word for taking something to be true, carrying no judgement on whether the acceptance was earned.

members.gloss: believe to be the case
members.tone: Softer than *believe*: it presents the belief as settled information one has come by, which lets the speaker hold it lightly.

members.gloss: believe or accept without questioning or challenge
members.tone: Disparaging of the believer rather than the claim, since the gloss builds the absence of questioning into the acceptance itself.

members.gloss: believe to be the case
members.tone: Formal, and it frames the belief as arrived at rather than merely held, giving it a footing *believe* does not claim.

families.axis: the person had a price → the payment named as the offence

members.gloss: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
members.tone: The plain word for a purchase turned on a person, so the contempt lies in the implication - they had a price - where *bribe* states the illegality outright.

members.gloss: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
members.tone: Names the payment as the offence it is, an accusation rather than the sardonic understatement of *buy*.

families.axis: plain originator of an institution → revered progenitor of it

members.gloss: a person who founds or establishes some institution
members.tone: Reverent - it casts the one who established the institution as its progenitor, giving the thing founded a lineage and the founder a claim on gratitude.

members.gloss: a person who founds or establishes some institution
members.tone: Flat and unadorned - it credits the act of starting an institution and stops there, without the honour *father* confers on the same person.

families.axis: bare classification by sex → a person defined by her tie to a particular man

members.gloss: a female person who plays a significant role (wife or mistress or girlfriend) in the life of a particular man
members.tone: Fixes a person by her attachment to one man and leaves the exact tie open — wife, mistress or girlfriend all answer to it — which is the possessive edge *female* has none of.

members.gloss: a youthful female person
members.tone: Marks youth and nothing else, saying nothing about who she is to anyone, unlike *woman* here.

members.gloss: a person who belongs to the sex that can have babies
members.tone: Flat classification by the sex that bears children, carrying neither the age of *girl* nor the relational claim of *woman*.

families.axis: someone who is simply often in your company → someone cherished and confided in

members.gloss: a person you know well and regard with affection and trust
members.tone: The plain, unhedged word for the bond, holding affection and trust together where *associate* names only the company kept.

members.gloss: a person regarded very fondly
members.tone: Pure fondness raised as high as the family goes, prizing the person without saying anything about trust or shared company.

members.gloss: informal term for a friend of the same sex
members.tone: Informal and easy, and it specifies a friend of the same sex where *friend* leaves that unsaid.

members.gloss: a close friend who accompanies their buddies in their activities
members.tone: Measures closeness in activities shared with a whole set of buddies, so the friendship is company kept rather than confidences given as in *intimate*.

members.gloss: a close friend who accompanies their buddies in their activities
members.tone: Openly affectionate for the same close, always-along friend, where *crony* leaves the fondness unspoken.

members.gloss: a friend who is frequently in the company of another
members.tone: The coolest of the words for frequent company, recording the habit and withholding any verdict on the affection behind it.

members.gloss: someone to whom private matters are confided
members.tone: Defines the friend entirely by what may be told them, making closeness a matter of trusted secrets rather than time spent together as in *companion*.
